text:
lena: heads-up: customer saw duplicate 'create-profile' records after a token refresh raced with a 429. using python quickstart. logs attached (redacted).
jon: can you paste the snippet + sdk version?
lena: python quickstart v0.9.2. snippet: 
```
WARN POST /v1/profiles 429 {"retry_after":0.3}
DEBUG refresh token start
INFO retrying POST /v1/profiles id=null
INFO POST /v1/profiles 201 id=prof_123
```
jon: that's an unsafe replay. without Idempotency-Key the server treats the retry as a new create.
sahil: quick mitigation: sampleapp should show adding an Idempotency-Key header for mutating calls. also SDKs should use exp backoff + full jitter to avoid synchronized retries. node/go already ship helpers; python lacks parity.
marco: decision question: default SDK behaviour = auto-idempotency or opt-in? my vote: opt-in + helper. auto-idemp can change app semantics.
jon: agree. default: exponential backoff w/ full jitter + NOT auto-idempotency. add helper: client.create_profile(..., idempotency_key=None) and sampleapp snippet: 
```python
import uuid
headers={"Authorization":f"Bearer {t}","Idempotency-Key":str(uuid.uuid4())}
resp=requests.post(url,json=body,headers=headers)
```
lena: i'll open a tiny PR to the quickstart showing header injection, add a short onboarding note about token-refresh + 429 races, and file a ticket for python SDK parity.
ci-bot: created ticket INT-2233 python-sdk-idempotency-parity and draft PR at github.com/redwood/sampleapp/pull/117
sahil: also add an e2e test that simulates a 429 during refresh to prevent regressions.
lena: tagging follow-up; will post PR + test links when ready. :thumbsup:
